text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Sam Nujoma announced on Wendesday that written permission from the police was necessary before any public demonstrations or marches.

- Namibia's Judge President Johan Strydom ruled out a judicial inquiry into allegations of bribery involving court officials. The charges were levelled by one of the accused in a multi-million dollar Katutura township housing fraud scam.

- The first presidential decree since independence has put a stop to a wave of illegal demonstrations and strikes in the country. Citizens have been forbidden to hold public demonstrations without the written approval of the police.
